facts.text: Piketon, originally called Jefferson, served as Pike County’s seat from 1815 until 1845 when the county moved to Waverly.
Robert Lucas, Ohio’s twelfth governor and Iowa’s first territorial governor, grew up in the area that became Piketon.
The village is best known for its uranium enrichment plant, one of only three such facilities in the United States.
Visitors can marvel at detailed model trains and then explore the adjacent museum that showcases railroad history and artifacts.
Dogwood Pass Old West Town offers a family‑friendly living‑history experience with reenactments and historic buildings open most weekends.
Piketon briefly appeared in the 2013 film White House Down, where a scene shows a missile launch from the local plant.
